hints: Think about what all addition polymers are like in the environment, with their long, strong carbon-carbon backbones.
Recall that PVC contains C, H and Cl, so complete combustion must give oxides of carbon and hydrogen plus a chlorine-containing acid gas.
Decide whether chlorine forms $\text{Cl}_2$ or combines with hydrogen when H atoms are available in the fuel and in the air moisture.
walkthrough:
**Recall the structure of PVC**

PVC is poly(chloroethene), made by addition polymerisation of chloroethene. Think of a very long saturated chain.

Monomer: $\text{CH}_2=\text{CHCl}$

Polymer repeat unit: $(-\text{CH}_2-\text{CHCl}-)_n$

**Decide the rate of biodegradation**

Like all addition polymers, PVC has only strong C-C and C-H and C-Cl single bonds. There are no polar C-O or C-N links that water or enzymes can easily attack.

So microorganisms cannot break it down. Biodegradation in landfill is very slow, which is why disposal is a problem.

**Predict the combustion gases**

Complete combustion in excess oxygen converts each element to its oxide or stable hydride. Carbon gives carbon dioxide and hydrogen gives water.

$$\text{C} \rightarrow \text{CO}_2, \quad \text{H} \rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

Chlorine does not stay as $\text{Cl}_2$ when H is present. It forms hydrogen chloride gas:
$$\text{Cl} + \text{H} \rightarrow \text{HCl}$$

So the gases are $\text{CO}_2$, $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ and $\text{HCl}$.

**Choose the correct row**

Slow biodegradation plus $\text{CO}_2$, $\text{H}_2\text{O}$, $\text{HCl}$ matches only one row of the table.

options.A: Incorrect. The gases $\text{CO}_2$, $\text{H}_2\text{O}$, $\text{HCl}$ are right, but biodegradation is not fast. PVC has an unreactive addition-polymer backbone with no hydrolysable groups, so microbes cannot digest it quickly.
options.B: Incorrect on both parts. Biodegradation is slow, not fast, and combustion does not give $\text{Cl}_2$. With plenty of H in the polymer, chlorine forms $\text{HCl}$.
options.C: Half correct. Slow biodegradation is right, but $\text{Cl}_2$ is wrong. Students often guess $\text{Cl}_2$ because PVC contains Cl, but in a hydrocarbon flame the Cl atoms pick up H to make acidic $\text{HCl}$ gas.
options.D: Correct. PVC is non-biodegradable so breakdown in landfill is slow. On complete combustion, C forms $\text{CO}_2$, H forms $\text{H}_2\text{O}$, and Cl forms toxic acidic $\text{HCl}$ gas.
